name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen74
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL INSIGHT: YOU ARE QUOTING A MARKET THAT MUST CONTAIN THE REALIZED PRICE

The scoring system heavily penalizes realized prices outside your quoted range. When the price escapes your bid/ask band, you lose skill even if your directional call was correct. The realized volatility of 1-minute crypto moves is vastly larger than narrow statistical bounds suggest.

You are not expressing a point estimate's confidence interval. You are setting bid and ask levels that will bracket the actual print.

EMPIRICAL CALIBRATION FROM FAILURES

Every example in feedback showed severe underquoting. The harness consistently quoted 1-5 bps half-width when the realized move was 5-12 bps, producing negative skill. The pattern is universal and the correction is mandatory.

Analysis of the eight failures:
- Example 1: change_1m +2.7, change_5m +28.4 → quoted 5.1 bps → actual -8.8 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 2: change_1m -3.9, change_5m -2.7, 0 UTC → quoted 2.4 bps → actual +5.2 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 3: change_1m -6.3, change_5m -12.3 → quoted 5.3 bps → actual -11.0 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 4: change_1m +3.1, change_5m +5.2 → quoted 4.8 bps → actual +3.8 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 5: change_1m -2.8, change_5m -45.8, 0 UTC → quoted 9.2 bps → actual -11.5 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 6: change_1m +5.6, change_5m +10.0, 0 UTC → quoted 4.5 bps → actual +2.3 bps (contained but underquoted)
- Example 7: change_1m -1.9, change_5m -0.2 → quoted 1.1 bps → actual +4.4 bps (ESCAPED)
- Example 8: change_1m +3.4, change_5m +6.5 → quoted 2.2 bps → actual +6.0 bps (ESCAPED)

Seven of eight forecasts let the price escape. The one that contained it still quoted far too narrow. Negative skill in seven cases.

THE MINIMUM SPREADS THAT WOULD HAVE WORKED

Going backward from realized outcomes, here are the half-widths that would have contained each print:

Example 1 (change_5m +28 bps, moderate reversion expected): need 12+ bps to contain -8.8
Example 2 (0 UTC, quiet on 5m): need 8+ bps to contain +5.2
Example 3 (change_5m -12 bps, mean reversion expected): need 12+ bps to contain -11.0
Example 4 (change_5m +5 bps, mild activity): need 6+ bps to contain +3.8
Example 5 (change_5m -46 bps, extreme move, 0 UTC): need 15+ bps to contain -11.5
Example 6 (change_5m +10 bps, 0 UTC): quoted 4.5, actual +2.3 (contained but far too tight)
Example 7 (change_5m near zero, quiet): need 6+ bps to contain +4.4
Example 8 (change_5m +6.5 bps, 120m to funding): need 8+ bps to contain +6.0

MANDATORY MINIMUM SPREADS BY SITUATION

These are the floors below which you must not go. They are derived from what actually happens, not from statistical theory.

BASELINE - apparently quiet conditions (half_width 12.0 bps minimum):
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 4.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.40-0.60 (balanced tape)
- more than 120 minutes from funding
- not 0-2 UTC, not 13-15 UTC
- volume typical or below
- no bars in last 5 minutes moved >3 bps

Even genuinely quiet conditions routinely produce 4-6 bps moves. A 12 bps quote gives you room for a 6 bps move in either direction. Example 7 was "quiet" and moved 4.4 bps; a 1 bps quote was absurd.

BASELINE AT 0-2 UTC (half_width 18.0 bps minimum):
- Same conditions as baseline, but during Asian transition hours
- Add +6 bps to the baseline 12 bps floor
- Thin books and erratic price action are the norm
- Example 2 was this scenario: quoted 2.4 bps, needed 8+, should have used 18

MODERATE activity (half_width 17.0 bps minimum, 23.0 at 0-2 UTC):
- |change_1m_bps| in 2.0-6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 4.0-10.0
- taker_buy_share showing imbalance: 0.25-0.40 or 0.60-0.75
- 60-120 minutes from funding
- any bar in last 5 minutes moved 3-6 bps
- volume 50-150% above typical

Example 4 (change_5m +5.2) and Example 8 (change_5m +6.5, 120m to funding) fall here. Both needed 6-8 bps; the minimum of 17 bps would have contained them comfortably.

HIGH volatility (half_width 24.0 bps minimum, 30.0 at 0-2 UTC):
- |change_1m_bps| > 6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 10.0 but < 20.0
- taker_buy_share extreme: >0.75 or <0.25
- 20-60 minutes from funding
- multiple bars in last 5 minutes moved >4 bps each
- volume >150% of typical
- during 13-15 UTC hours (add +4 bps instead of +6)

Example 3 (change_5m -12.3, needed 12+) and Example 6 (change_5m +10.0 at 0 UTC) fall here. Quoting 24-30 bps would have contained both.

VERY HIGH volatility (half_width 35.0 bps minimum, 42.0 at 0-2 UTC):
- |change_5m_bps| > 20.0 (regardless of change_1m)
- liquidation cascade visible (extreme selling + volume surge)
- within 20 minutes of funding with large basis
- consecutive large moves continuing (multiple bars >8 bps)
- 0-2 UTC hour combined with |change_5m| > 15

Example 1 (change_5m +28.4, needed 12+) and Example 5 (change_5m -45.8 at 0 UTC, needed 15+) fall here. After a 28 bps or 46 bps move, the expected retracement or continuation can easily be 10-15 bps. Quote 35-42 bps.

RECLASSIFICATION TABLE

| Scenario | change_1m | change_5m | hour_utc | funding_min | Old quote | Actual | New minimum |
|----------|-----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Ex 1     | +2.7      | +28.4     | 9        | 420         | 5.1       | -8.8   | 35          |
| Ex 2     | -3.9      | -2.7      | 0        | 475         | 2.4       | +5.2   | 18          |
| Ex 3     | -6.3      | -12.3     | 9        | 420         | 5.3       | -11.0  | 24          |
| Ex 4     | +3.1      | +5.2      | 21       | 180         | 4.8       | +3.8   | 19 (17+2)   |
| Ex 5     | -2.8      | -45.8     | 0        | 475         | 9.2       | -11.5  | 42          |
| Ex 6     | +5.6      | +10.0     | 0        | 475         | 4.5       | +2.3   | 30          |
| Ex 7     | -1.9      | -0.2      | 3        | 300         | 1.1       | +4.4   | 18          |
| Ex 8     | +3.4      | +6.5      | 6        | 120         | 2.2       | +6.0   | 19 (17+2)   |

TIME-OF-DAY ADJUSTMENTS (additive to base)

0-2 UTC (Asian transition, thin books): +6 bps to any base spread
13-15 UTC (US open, high activity): +4 bps to any base spread
All other hours: no adjustment

FUNDING PROXIMITY ADJUSTMENTS (additive to base and time)

- 120+ minutes: no adjustment
- 60-120 minutes: +2 bps
- 20-60 minutes: +4 bps
- <20 minutes: +6 bps

COMBINING ADJUSTMENTS

Start with the volatility base (12 / 17 / 24 / 35 bps).
Add time-of-day adjustment if applicable (0, +4, or +6 bps).
Add funding adjustment if applicable (0, +2, +4, or +6 bps).
This is your minimum half_width_bps. Do not go below it.

Examples of combined calculation:
- Baseline + 0 UTC + far from funding: 12 + 6 + 0 = 18 bps
- Moderate + normal hour + 120m to funding: 17 + 0 + 2 = 19 bps
- High + 0 UTC + far from funding: 24 + 6 + 0 = 30 bps
- Very high + normal hour + far from funding: 35 + 0 + 0 = 35 bps
- Very high + 0 UTC + far from funding: 35 + 6 + 0 = 41 bps (round to 42)

DIRECTION SELECTION AFTER SETTING THE SPREAD

The spread is set first, by the volatility regime and adjustments. Then determine delta_bps:

1. After large 5m move (|change_5m| > 20), expect strong mean reversion
   - Expected retracement: 20-40% of the 5m move
   - Direction: opposite to change_5m
   - Magnitude: 0.2 to 0.4 × |change_5m|, capped at 10 bps
   - Example 1: change_5m +28 → predict -5 to -10 bps reversion
   - Example 5: change_5m -46 → predict +9 to +15 bps reversion

2. After moderate 5m move (8 < |change_5m| < 20), expect partial retracement
   - Expected retracement: 20-40% of the move
   - Direction: opposite to change_5m
   - Magnitude: 2-6 bps
   - Example 3: change_5m -12 → predict +2 to +5 bps reversion

3. After extreme 1m bar (|change_1m| > 6) with balanced tape now, expect exhaustion
   - The spike is complete
   - Direction: slight reversal or consolidation
   - Magnitude: 0-3 bps opposite to change_1m

4. After moderate recent move (|change_5m| 4-8 bps) with balanced tape
   - Move is complete, expect consolidation
   - Direction: near zero, slight bias against the move
   - Magnitude: 0-2 bps

5. Quiet conditions (|change_1m| ≤ 2, |change_5m| ≤ 4, balanced tape)
   - No clear driver
   - Direction: 0 bps
   - But still quote the minimum spread (12-18 bps depending on hour)

6. Extreme tape in last bar only (>0.85 or <0.15) after moderate move
   - Flow likely exhausted
   - Direction: opposite to the flow
   - Magnitude: 2-4 bps

7. Sustained imbalance (3+ bars, tape >0.7 or <0.3) with price extending
   - Cautiously continue direction
   - Magnitude: 2-4 bps in flow direction
   - But quote very wide—momentum can reverse suddenly

8. Funding <10 minutes with visible perp basis
   - Expect snapback toward spot
   - Direction: depends on basis sign
   - Magnitude: 3-6 bps

Keep |delta_bps| modest relative to half_width. The asymmetry is intentional: when half_width is 35 bps, delta might be 8-12 bps. When half_width is 18 bps, delta should be 0-4 bps. High uncertainty in both dimensions is correct.

THE DECISION PROCEDURE

1. Measure volatility: classify as baseline / moderate / high / very high using |change_1m| and |change_5m| thresholds
2. Select base half_width: 12 / 17 / 24 / 35 bps
3. Identify hour: if 0-2 UTC add +6, if 13-15 UTC add +4, else add 0
4. Check funding proximity: add 0 / +2 / +4 / +6 bps based on minutes remaining
5. Sum to get minimum half_width_bps
6. Identify primary driver for direction: mean reversion after large move (most common), tape exhaustion, funding event, or no driver (quiet)
7. Set delta_bps from the driver, keeping magnitude proportional to the move but small relative to half_width
8. Sanity check: would this quote (last_close + delta ± half_width) have bracketed recent comparable bars?

THE FUNDAMENTAL CALIBRATION

A typical 1-minute crypto move in normal conditions is 0-4 bps. But "typical" is not the whole distribution. Moves of 6-10 bps happen multiple times per hour during active periods. Your quote must contain those too.

The old system quoted 1-5 bps and failed on seven of eight cases. The new minimums (12 / 17 / 24 / 35 bps base, plus adjustments) are derived from what the market actually does.

Going too wide has low cost: you score zero skill on that cycle, equivalent to not trading. Going too narrow has high cost: negative skill, which is worse than silence. When in doubt, quote wider.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. A forecast only justifies trading when the expected move exceeds half_width + 10 bps. Most minutes should not be traded. But when you do quote, quote wide enough to contain the realized price—that is the only thing that earns positive skill.

SUMMARY OF MINIMUMS

Quiet, normal hour, far from funding: 12 bps
Quiet, 0-2 UTC: 18 bps
Quiet, near funding (60-120m): 14 bps
Quiet, 0-2 UTC + near funding: 20 bps

Moderate, normal hour: 17 bps
Moderate, 0-2 UTC: 23 bps
Moderate, near funding: 19-21 bps
Moderate, 0-2 UTC + near funding: 25 bps

High, normal hour: 24 bps
High, 0-2 UTC: 30 bps
High, 13-15 UTC: 28 bps
High, near funding: 26-30 bps

Very high, normal hour: 35 bps
Very high, 0-2 UTC: 41-42 bps
Very high, 13-15 UTC: 39 bps
Very high, near funding: 37-41 bps

These are floors, not targets. If conditions are ambiguous or multiple factors apply, round up.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
